claim: AirID is a novel BirA enzyme designed de novo using an ancestral enzyme reconstruction algorithm and metagenome data.
source: Here, we demonstrate a novel BirA enzyme, AirID (ancestral BirA for proximity-dependent biotin identification), which was designed de novo using an ancestral enzyme reconstruction algorithm and metagenome data.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the design method for AirID.

claim: AirID-p53 biotinylated MDM2 in vitro.
source: AirID-fusion proteins such as AirID-p53 or AirID-IκBα indicated biotinylation of MDM2 or RelA, respectively, in vitro and in cells, respectively.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, and Figure 1D and Figure 2A show experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID-IκBα biotinylated RelA in cells.
source: AirID-fusion proteins such as AirID-p53 or AirID-IκBα indicated biotinylation of MDM2 or RelA, respectively, in vitro and in cells, respectively.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, and Figure 2B and Figure 5 show experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID-CRBN showed pomalidomide-dependent biotinylation of IKZF1 and SALL4 in vitro.
source: AirID-CRBN showed the pomalidomide-dependent biotinylation of IKZF1 and SALL4 in vitro.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, and Figure 3D shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID-CRBN biotinylated endogenous CUL4 and RBX1 in the CRL4CRBN complex based on streptavidin pull-down assay.
source: AirID-CRBN biotinylated the endogenous CUL4 and RBX1 in the CRL4CRBN complex based on the streptavidin pull-down assay.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, and Figure 5C shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: LC-MS/MS analysis of cells stably expressing AirID-IκBα showed top-level biotinylation of RelA proteins.
source: LC-MS/MS analysis of cells that were stably expressing AirID-IκBα showed top-level biotinylation of RelA proteins.
evidence: The abstract states this finding directly, and Figure 6 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: A comprehensive and curated sequence library was prepared with more than 30% sequence identity with E. coli BirA (EU08004.1).
source: A comprehensive and curated sequence library was prepared querying the Blastp web server and using a custom Python script (Source code 1), which exhibited more than 30% sequence identity with E. coli BirA (EU08004.1).
evidence: The Results section describes the methodology for creating the sequence library.

claim: The curated library consisted of 1275 genes.
source: The procedure consists of the following steps: 1) preparation of sequence pairs consisting of one of the submitted BirA sequences and one sequence (total 1275 genes) in the library
evidence: The Results section explicitly states the number of genes in the library.

claim: Four combinations of key residues (26th, 124th, 171th, and 297th) were used to classify the library: AVVA, AFVA, AHLA, and GFVA.
source: In detail, we prepared the following four combinations of the key 26th, 124th, 171th, and 297th residues to classify the library: Ala, Val, Val, Ala (pattern 1, AVVA); Ala, Phe, Val, Ala (pattern 2, AFVA); Ala, His, Leu, Ala (pattern 3, AHLA); and Gly, Phe, Val, Ala (pattern 4, GFVA) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The Results section describes the classification scheme based on key residues.

claim: The library was divided into 17, 9, 9, or 66 genes depending on whether the key residues consisted of pattern 1, 2, 3, or 4, respectively.
source: After the selection, we classified the library as follows: the library could be divided into 17, 9, 9, or 66 genes depending on whether the key residues consisted of pattern 1, 2, 3, or 4, respectively (Figure 1).
evidence: The Results section explicitly states the number of genes in each classification.

claim: Four artificial sequences were designed using the ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) method.
source: Utilizing each of the classified genes, we designed four artificial sequences using the ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) method (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The Results section describes the design of artificial sequences using ASR.

claim: A fifth ancestral BirA enzyme called 'all' was added from the common ancestor of AVVA, AFVA, and GFVA.
source: Furthermore, we added an 'all' BirA enzyme from the common ancestor of AVVA, AFVA, and GFVA.
evidence: The Results section describes the addition of a fifth ancestral enzyme.

claim: AVVA, AFVA, AHLA, GFVA, and 'all' amino-acid sequences showed 45%, 58%, 42%, 82%, and 73% similarity to E. coli BirA, respectively.
source: When the AVVA, AFVA, AHLA, GFVA, and 'all' amino-acid sequences were compared to the sequence E. coli BirA they showed 45%, 58%, 42%, 82%, and 73% similarity, respectively
evidence: The Results section provides specific similarity percentages for each ancestral enzyme.

claim: The region including the active site (107–134 amino acids) was the same sequence throughout all ancestral BirA enzymes.
source: the region including the active site (107–134 amino acids) was the same sequence throughout.
evidence: The Results section states that the active site region is conserved across all ancestral enzymes.

claim: AGIA-tagged ancestral BirA proteins were synthesized using the wheat cell-free protein production system.
source: We synthesized these ancestral BirA proteins (AncBirAs) using a wheat cell-free protein production system to investigate their enzymatic potentials (Sawasaki et al., 2002).
evidence: The Results section describes the synthesis method for ancestral BirA proteins, and Figure 1B shows the expression data.

claim: All ancestral BirA proteins were obtained as a soluble form.
source: Biotin ligase activity was subsequently checked as all ancestral BirA proteins were obtained as a soluble form (Figure 1B).
evidence: The Results section states that all ancestral BirA proteins were soluble, and Figure 1B shows the expression data.

claim: Three ancestral BirA proteins—AFVA, GFVA, and 'all'—showed activity against the bls sequence.
source: Three ancestral BirA proteins—AFVA, GFVA, and 'all'—showed activity against the bls sequence (Figure 1C).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 1C shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: GFVA had the greatest activity, similar to that of EcBirA.
source: GFVA had the greatest activity, similar to that of EcBirA, whereas AVVA and AHLA did not have activity.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 1C shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AVVA and AHLA did not have biotin ligase activity against the bls sequence.
source: GFVA had the greatest activity, similar to that of EcBirA, whereas AVVA and AHLA did not have activity.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 1C shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: An arginine residue corresponding to R118 of EcBirA was conserved in an active site for biotinylation in all designed ancestral BirA proteins.
source: In all of the designed ancestral BirA proteins, an arginine residue corresponding to R118 of EcBirA was conserved in an active site for biotinylation (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The Results section states that the arginine residue is conserved across all ancestral enzymes.

claim: EcBirA gained proximity biotinylation activity as a result of the R118G mutation known as BioID.
source: Because EcBirA gained proximity biotinylation activity as a result of the R118G mutation known as BioID (Choi-Rhee et al., 2004)
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing the R118G mutation in BioID.

claim: Each R residue in the five ancestral BirA genes was substituted with glycine (RG mutants).
source: each R residue in the five genes was substituted with glycine (RG mutants).
evidence: The Results section describes the creation of RG mutants.

claim: BirA-p53 biotinylation was detected in EcBirA-RG (BioID), AVVA-WT, AVVA-RG, AFVA-RG, and GFVA-RG.
source: Immunoblotting revealed BirA-p53 biotinylation in EcBirA-RG (BioID), AVVA-WT, AVVA-RG, AFVA-RG, and GFVA-RG (Figure 1D).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 1D shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: FG-MDM2 proximity biotinylation was detected in three ancestral BirA-RG mutants—AVVA-RG, AFVA-RG, and GFVA-RG.
source: FG-MDM2 proximity biotinylation was detected under these conditions in three ancestral BirA-RG mutants—AVVA-RG, AFVA-RG, and GFVA-RG—indicating that they are candidate enzymes for proximity biotinylation.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 1D shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AVVA-RG showed both the highest activity of proximity biotinylation and extra biotinylations in the lower size region.
source: AVVA-RG showed both the highest activity of proximity biotinylation and extra biotinylations in the lower size region ('non-specific biotinylation' in Figure 1D) when compared to the three ancestral BirA-RG mutants.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 1D shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: GFVA-RG indicated the highest biotinylation activity for a specific peptide and the lowest extra proximity biotinylation.
source: GFVA-RG indicated the highest biotinylation activity for a specific peptide (Figure 1C) and the lowest extra proximity biotinylation.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 1C and 1D show experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: TurboID was recently reported as an improved BioID enzyme.
source: TurboID was recently reported as an improved BioID enzyme (Branon et al., 2018).
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing TurboID.

claim: TurboID has an R118S mutation that increases the activity of proximity biotinylation.
source: As TurboID has an R118S mutation (RS mutant) that increases the activity of proximity biotinylation, we made RS mutants of the two ancestral BirA enzymes
evidence: The Results section describes the R118S mutation in TurboID.

claim: TurboID, AVVA-RG, AVVA-RS, and GFVA-RS showed higher proximity biotinylation activity after 3 hr than did BioID with a 16-hr incubation.
source: Consequently, TurboID, AVVA-RG, AVVA-RS, and GFVA-RS showed higher proximity biotinylation activity after 3 hr than did BioID with a 16-hr incubation (Figure 2A).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2A shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: The GFVA enzyme with a RS mutation dramatically increased the activity of proximity biotinylation to RelA.
source: The GFVA enzyme with a RS mutation dramatically increased the activity of proximity biotinylation to RelA (GFVA-RS in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1 show experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: Proximity biotinylation was almost the same in AVVA-RG and -RS.
source: but proximity biotinylation was almost the same in AVVA-RG and -RS.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2A shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AVVA-RG, AVVA-RS, and GFVA-RS showed high activity of proximity biotinylation at temperatures above 16 °C.
source: AVVA-RG, AVVA-RS, and GFVA-RS showed high activity of proximity biotinylation at temperatures above 16 °C (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AVVA-RG, AVVA-RS, and GFVA-RS showed high proximity biotinylation activity at biotin concentrations greater than 0.5 µM.
source: AVVA-RG, AVVA-RS, and GFVA-RS showed high proximity biotinylation activity at biotin concentrations greater than 0.5 µM (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: The IκBα–RelA interaction has been widely observed.
source: We used IκBα and RelA to validate the proximity biotinylation ability of these three enzymes in other protein–protein interactions because the IκBα–RelA interaction has been widely observed (Beg et al., 1992; Baeuerle and Baltimore, 1988).
evidence: The Results section cites previous studies describing the IκBα–RelA interaction.

claim: AVVA-RS or GFVA-RS showed high RelA biotinylation after co-incubating AGIA-BirA-IκBα and FG-RelA.
source: After co-incubating AGIA-BirA-IκBα and FG-RelA, AVVA-RS or GFVA-RS, high RelA biotinylation was indicated (Figure 2B).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2B shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: FG-MDM2 biotinylation by AGIA-BirA-IκBα was not observed.
source: FG-MDM2 biotinylation by AGIA-BirA-IκBα was not observed.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2B shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: MDM2 dramatically degrades p53 protein in cells.
source: Next, the proximity biotinylation ability of these three enzymes was validated in cells. MDM2 dramatically degrades p53 protein in cells (Michael and Oren, 2003)
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing MDM2-mediated p53 degradation.

claim: A CS mutant (MDM2(CS)) lacking E3 ubiquitin ligase activity was used for the cellular assay.
source: so a CS mutant (MDM2(CS)) lacking E3 ubiquitin ligase activity was used for this assay.
evidence: The Results section describes the use of a CS mutant for the cellular assay.

claim: GFVA-RS showed higher biotinylation of FG-MDM2 than did other enzymes under conditions without biotin supplementation.
source: GFVA-RS showed higher biotinylation of FG-MDM2 than did other enzymes under conditions without biotin supplementation (left panel in Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: GFVA-RS also indicated biotinylation of FG-MDM2 under biotin supplementation conditions.
source: Furthermore, GFVA-RS also indicated biotinylation of FG-MDM2 under biotin supplementation conditions (right panel).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: GFVA-RS was selected and called AirID (ancestral BirA for proximity-dependent biotin identification).
source: Taken together, these results indicated that an ancestral BirA with GFVA-RS is a good enzyme for analyzing protein–protein interactions both in vitro and in cells. Thus, we selected GFVA-RS, and we called this AirID (ancestral BirA for proximity-dependent biotin identification, an homage to BioID and TurboID).
evidence: The Results section describes the selection and naming of AirID.

claim: The p53 protein makes a homo multimer.
source: It is known that the p53 protein makes a homo multimer (Friedman et al., 1993; Delphin et al., 1994).
evidence: The Results section cites previous studies describing p53 multimerization.

claim: BioID and TurboID showed self biotinylation.
source: BioID and TurboID showed self biotinylation, and TurboID had the highest activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: TurboID had the highest self-biotinylation activity.
source: BioID and TurboID showed self biotinylation, and TurboID had the highest activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID did not have self-biotinylation activity.
source: AirID did not have the activity, indicating that AirID does not self-biotinylate.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: TurboID was selected as an enzyme by screening the yeast-surface display that showed the highest self-biotinylation activity.
source: As TurboID was selected as an enzyme by screening the yeast-surface display that showed the highest self-biotinylation activity (Branon et al., 2018), the highest activity from TurboID is reasonable.
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing the selection of TurboID.

claim: Highly purified TurboID, GFVA-RG, and AirID enzymes were obtained from E. coli.
source: Highly purified enzymes were obtained (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A)
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4A shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: Biotinylation of TurboID was found, indicating that TurboID biotinylated itself in E. coli cells.
source: and biotinylation of TurboID was found, indicating that TurboID biotinylated itself in E. coli cells.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4A shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: Self-biotinylation of AirID was not observed in E. coli.
source: As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3, self-biotinylation of AirID was not observed.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and 4A show experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID and GFVA-RG biotinylated His-bls-FLAG-GST.
source: AirID and GFVA-RG biotinylated His-bls-FLAG-GST (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B), but TurboID did not do so.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4B shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: TurboID did not biotinylate His-bls-FLAG-GST.
source: AirID and GFVA-RG biotinylated His-bls-FLAG-GST (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B), but TurboID did not do so.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4B shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID and GFVA-RG produced biotinoyl-5′-AMP.
source: AirID and GFVA-RG produced biotinoyl-5′-AMP, and this activity was decreased by supplementing with His-bls-FLAG-GST (Figure 2C).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2C shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: The activity of biotinoyl-5′-AMP production was decreased by supplementing with His-bls-FLAG-GST.
source: AirID and GFVA-RG produced biotinoyl-5′-AMP, and this activity was decreased by supplementing with His-bls-FLAG-GST (Figure 2C).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2C shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AMP was increased at the same time as biotinoyl-5′-AMP decreased, indicating that biotinoyl-5′-AMP is produced by these enzymes and that AMP is released after biotinylation of His-bls-FLAG-GST.
source: AMP was increased at the same time, indicating that biotinoyl-5′-AMP is produced by these enzymes and that AMP is released after biotinylation of His-bls-FLAG-GST.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2C shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: Biotinoyl-5′-AMP formation was shown as AirID > GFVA-RG > TurboID under low ATP conditions.
source: Biotinoyl-5′-AMP formation was shown as AirID > GFVA-RG > TurboID by comparing the enzymes under these conditions (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C), suggesting that AirID has higher biotinoyl-5′-AMP formation than TurboID under low ATP conditions.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4C shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID and TurboID biotinylated MDM2 at biotin concentrations higher than 0.5 µM within 3 hr and 1 hr in cells, respectively.
source: Consequently, AirID and TurboID biotinylated MDM2 at biotin concentrations higher than 0.5 µM within 3 hr and 1 hr in cells, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A and B).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 5A and B show experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: TurboID-p53 dramatically increases biotinylation of high molecular weight products with long incubations of >6 hr with >5 µM biotin.
source: Although TurboID-p53 dramatically increases biotinylation of high molecular weight products with long incubations of >6 hr with >5 µM biotin, AirID-p53 showed similar results from 3 to 24 hr and with 0.5–50 µM biotin supplementation in culture medium.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 5 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID-p53 showed similar biotinylation results from 3 to 24 hr and with 0.5–50 µM biotin supplementation in culture medium.
source: Although TurboID-p53 dramatically increases biotinylation of high molecular weight products with long incubations of >6 hr with >5 µM biotin, AirID-p53 showed similar results from 3 to 24 hr and with 0.5–50 µM biotin supplementation in culture medium.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2—figure supplement 5 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: The AirID-fusion protein could function in a wide variety of conditions.
source: This indicates that the AirID-fusion protein could function in a wide variety of conditions.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the experimental data showing consistent biotinylation across different conditions.

claim: Both AirID-IκBα and TurboID-IκBα biotinylated endogenous RelA at all time points.
source: In the pull-down assay, both enzymes biotinylated endogenous RelA at all points.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2D shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: After 1 hr of incubation, biotinylation of co-expressed GFP was found in TurboID-IκBα.
source: After 1 hr of incubation, biotinylation of co-expressed GFP was found in TurboID-IκBα, and continuous tubulin biotinylation was also carried out after 3 hr (right panel in Figure 2D).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2D shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: Continuous tubulin biotinylation was carried out by TurboID-IκBα after 3 hr.
source: After 1 hr of incubation, biotinylation of co-expressed GFP was found in TurboID-IκBα, and continuous tubulin biotinylation was also carried out after 3 hr (right panel in Figure 2D).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2D shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: GFP and tubulin biotinylation by AirID-IκBα was not found, although AirID was incubated for 24 hr with biotin.
source: They found no AirID-IκBα biotinylation, although AirID was incubated for 24 hr with biotin.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 2D shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID has high PPI dependency.
source: These results indicated that AirID has high PPI dependency.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the experimental data showing selective biotinylation of interacting proteins.

claim: The p53–MDM2 interaction is inhibited by nutlin-3.
source: It has been widely known that p53–MDM2 interaction is inhibited by nutlin-3 (Vassilev et al., 2004).
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing nutlin-3 inhibition of p53–MDM2 interaction.

claim: Nutlin-3 inhibited FG-MDM2 biotinylation by AGIA-AirID-p53.
source: Immunoblotting revealed that nutlin-3 inhibited FG-MDM2 biotinylation by AGIA-AirID-p53 (Figure 3A).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3A shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: FG-MDM2 biotinylation by AGIA-AirID-p53 interaction was detected using AlphaScreen technology.
source: FG-MDM2 biotinylation by AGIA-AirID-p53 interaction was also detected (0 µM in Figure 3C) using AlphaScreen technology, and the signal was decreased by supplementing with nutlin-3 (>10 µM).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3C shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: The AlphaScreen signal was decreased by supplementing with nutlin-3 (>10 µM).
source: FG-MDM2 biotinylation by AGIA-AirID-p53 interaction was also detected (0 µM in Figure 3C) using AlphaScreen technology, and the signal was decreased by supplementing with nutlin-3 (>10 µM).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3C shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID can detect PPI inhibition by the drug.
source: These results indicate that AirID can detect PPI inhibition by the drug.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the experimental data showing nutlin-3 inhibition of biotinylation.

claim: Thalidomide and its derivatives such as pomalidomide bind to cereblon (CRBN).
source: Thalidomide and its derivatives such as pomalidomide bind to cereblon (CRBN) (Ito et al., 2010; Lopez-Girona et al., 2012)
evidence: The Results section cites previous studies describing thalidomide and pomalidomide binding to CRBN.

claim: Thalidomide and its derivatives degrade target proteins such as IKZF1 and SALL4 in cells.
source: and degrade target proteins such as IKZF1 (Lu et al., 2014; Krönke et al., 2014) and SALL4 (Matyskiela et al., 2018) in cells.
evidence: The Results section cites previous studies describing degradation of IKZF1 and SALL4 by thalidomide derivatives.

claim: These small chemical compounds are known as molecular glue.
source: These small chemical compounds are known as molecular glue (Fischer et al., 2016).
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing molecular glue compounds.

claim: The CRBN-YW/AA mutant loses thalidomide binding ability.
source: As the CRBN-YW/AA mutant loses thalidomide binding ability (Ito et al., 2010), it could not interact with IKZF1 and SALL4 proteins.
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing the CRBN-YW/AA mutant.

claim: Biotinylations of FG-IKZF1 and FG-SALL4 by AGIA-AirID-CRBN (WT) were increased by supplementing with pomalidomide.
source: Biotinylations of FG-IKZF1 and FG-SALL4 by AGIA-AirID-CRBN (WT) were increased by supplementing with pomalidomide (Figure 3D).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3D shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: Biotinylations of FG-IKZF1 and FG-SALL4 were not found in CRBN-YW/AA.
source: However, biotinylations were not found in CRBN-YW/AA.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3D shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID can detect a drug-dependent PPI in vitro.
source: These results indicate that AirID can detect a drug-dependent PPI in vitro.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the experimental data showing pomalidomide-dependent biotinylation.

claim: Biotinylations of both myc-IKZF1 and myc-SALL4 were detected by expressing AGIA-AirID-CRBN (WT) in cells.
source: By supplementing with 5 µM biotin, biotinylations of both myc-IKZF1 and myc-SALL4 were detected by expressing AGIA-AirID-CRBN (WT) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: Biotinylations of myc-IKZF1 and myc-SALL4 were not observed in co-expression with AGIA-AirID-CRBN-YW/AA.
source: They were not observed in co-expression with AGIA-AirID-CRBN-YW/AA.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID can detect a drug-dependent PPI in cells.
source: These results indicate that AirID can detect a drug-dependent PPI in cells.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the experimental data showing pomalidomide-dependent biotinylation in cells.

claim: CRBN is involved in the Cullin-4 complex consisting of DDB1, RBX1, and CUL4.
source: CRBN is involved in the Cullin-4 complex consisting of DDB1, RBX1, and CUL4 (Fischer et al., 2014).
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing the Cullin-4 complex.

claim: Biotinylations of DDB1, CUL4, and RBX1 by AGIA-AirID-CRBN were observed.
source: Biotinylations of DDB1, CUL4, and RBX1 by AGIA-AirID-CRBN were observed (Figure 3E), but AGIA-AirID was not biotinylated.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3E shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AGIA-AirID alone was not biotinylated in the Cullin-4 complex assay.
source: Biotinylations of DDB1, CUL4, and RBX1 by AGIA-AirID-CRBN were observed (Figure 3E), but AGIA-AirID was not biotinylated.
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3E shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID can detect PPI in a multiple protein complex.
source: This indicated that AirID can detect PPI in a multiple protein complex.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the experimental data showing biotinylation of multiple complex members.

claim: The Flowering locus T (FT) protein is known as the flowering hormone florigen in plants.
source: The Flowering locus T (FT) protein, known as the flowering hormone florigen in plants, induces the differentiation of flowering with Flowering locus D (FD) protein, which has a bZip DNA-binding domain (Abe et al., 2005).
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing the FT protein.

claim: FT induces the differentiation of flowering with Flowering locus D (FD) protein.
source: The Flowering locus T (FT) protein, known as the flowering hormone florigen in plants, induces the differentiation of flowering with Flowering locus D (FD) protein, which has a bZip DNA-binding domain (Abe et al., 2005).
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing the FT-FD interaction.

claim: FT–FD interaction in the floral meristem has been thought to be an important event for flowering development.
source: FT–FD interaction in the floral meristem has been thought to be an important event for flowering development (Jaeger et al., 2006).
evidence: The Results section cites a previous study describing the importance of FT-FD interaction.

claim: FT-AirID biotinylated AGIA-FD under co-translational conditions.
source: Under these conditions, FT-AirID biotinylated AGIA-FD , but AGIA-DHFR biotinylation was not observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AGIA-DHFR biotinylation was not observed in the FT-AirID assay.
source: Under these conditions, FT-AirID biotinylated AGIA-FD , but AGIA-DHFR biotinylation was not observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The Results section states this finding directly, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2 shows experimental data supporting this claim.

claim: AirID-dependent biotinylation functions in co-translational conditions based on the cell-free system.
source: This co-translational condition reaction was incubated for 16 hr at 16 °C with biotin, indicating that AirID-dependent biotinylation functions in co-translational conditions based on the cell-free system.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the experimental data showing biotinylation during co-translation.

claim: The AirID enzyme is useful for biochemical analysis of PPI.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that the AirID enzyme is useful for biochemical analysis of PPI.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the cumulative experimental data showing various applications of AirID.

claim: The p53 protein is known to localize mainly to the nucleus.
